acceptanceCriteria: A reviewed inventory selects which local records require authenticated encryption and binds every envelope to owner scope, record class and ID, schema, key ID, revision, algorithm suite, nonce, creation time, and payload digest without exposing health content in associated data.

Encryption uses a reviewed AEAD construction with unique nonces and platform-protected nonexportable key material; missing keys, duplicate nonces, unknown algorithms, invalid tags, future schemas, owner mismatch, rollback, and malformed ciphertext fail closed before plaintext is published.

Mutation and key rotation use an atomic old-or-new protocol with durable acknowledgement, resumable migration state, bounded rollback, crypto-shredding semantics, and no window where plaintext or a partially re-encrypted record is treated as current.

Fault and target-platform tests cover lost acknowledgement, process kill, concurrent writers, corrupted ciphertext, key invalidation, clock rollback, restore to another device, cross-account substitution, and recovery UX; encrypted-at-rest is never described as authentication, secure deletion proof, backup protection, or regulatory compliance.

items.title: Cryptographic inventory, agility, and deprecation gate

acceptanceCriteria: A generated, versioned inventory maps every application and dependency cryptographic primitive to purpose, algorithm and parameters, provider and version, key owner, storage, protected data, protocol role, export or backup behavior, call sites, and replacement owner; unknown or newly discovered use blocks release review.

A dated transition drill covers dependency and OS algorithm changes, provider removal, corrupted legacy data, unavailable migration tooling, and emergency deprecation while preserving user access through an explicit recovery path; post-quantum planning is inventory-driven and does not claim present quantum resistance.

items.title: Platform file-protection and implicit-backup attestation
items.currentGap: Android source policy now denies cloud backup and device transfer, but the release does not yet prove the merged or packaged rules on target devices, inventory every persisted path, or attest iOS and macOS file-protection, Keychain synchronization, app-container backup, and restore behavior. This implicit platform channel is distinct from the explicit encrypted user backup workflow.
acceptanceCriteria: A generated inventory binds every database, preference, cache, file, log, export, Keychain item, and Android storage domain to a reviewed sensitivity, file-protection class, backup and device-transfer policy, retention rule, owner, and artifact path; unclassified or newly discovered persistence fails the release.

Physical-device backup, restore, device-transfer, reinstall, locked-device, OS-upgrade, corrupted-backup, and account-switch drills show that health records and secret material are not restored through an undeclared channel, while explicit user-owned export remains separately previewed and consented.

Evidence binds artifact checksum, OS and device, account state, source and destination, expected and observed path sets, and cleanup result; vendor-specific behavior, unavailable probes, or incomplete enumeration is reported as unverified and cannot satisfy acceptance.

items.title: Backend location, retention, and residency contract

Every persisted collection, document family, authentication record, audit event, storage object, operator export, backup, and service log has an enforced owner, purpose, location, retention trigger, deletion path, legal-hold state, and verification query; absent or unverified behavior remains unknown rather than being labeled compliant.

Provisioning and deployment gates query actual service state and compare it with the reviewed manifest before writes are enabled, preserve immutable evidence for irreversible location choices, and fail closed on multi-region ambiguity, emulator credentials, default-project fallback, or stale operator output.

Expiry, account deletion, recent-authentication failure, partial backend outage, retry, acknowledgement loss, orphaned subcollection or object, and restoration tests prove bounded outcomes across all configured environments; the UI and public copy distinguish observed technical location and retention from legal residency or regulatory conclusions.
